Detailed Accident Reports (DAR) in case of death of - (i)
Tony; (ii) Tejas and bodily injury to (iii) Gaurav are taken up to be decided simultaneously.

Background 2. As gleaned from Final Report in FIR No.234/2022 PS Jaffarpur Kalan - Gaurav, Tony and Tejas returning home riding motorcycle No.DL-8SBH-9754 after attending marriage function MACT No.299/2023 Rakesh Kumar & Anr. Vs. Pawan Kumar & Anr. Page No. 3 of 25 at Radhey Shyam Vatika, Surhera, Delhi met with an accident near Dharampal Piyao, Mundhela Khurd Village, Delhi on 08.12.2022 at about 9:06 pm after their motorcycle was hit by White Colour Taxi No.
DL-1ZD-2211 coming from opposite side in rash and negligent manner.
They were shifted to RTRM Hospital, where Tony admitted upon MLC No.7304/22 was declared 'Brought Dead'.
His younger brother Tejas admitted upon MLC No.7302/22 was referred to Higher Centre but succumbed to injuries in course of treatment at Tarak Hospital, Dwarka Mor, Delhi.
3. FIR No.234/22 under section 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS Jaffarpur Kalan on 09.12.2022 and site-plan was prepared by IO.

Respondent Pawan Kumar produced by ASI Ranvir Singh, In-charge, PCR Van along with MLC No.7305/22 was formally arrested and released on police bail and dead bodies of Tony and Tejas were handed over to their relatives after identification and postmortem examination.

Documents viz. DL, RC, Fitness and Policy produced by respondent were verified from concerned authorities and offence under section 185 M.V. Act was added on the basis of MLC No.7305/22 of Pawan Kumar recording Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) 127 mg/ml.

Statement of Gaurav was recorded who alleged that White Taxi coming from opposite side hit their motorcycle on the left side of road and offence under section 338 IPC was also added on the basis of final opinion of grievous injury upon his MLC.

IO, thereafter, concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in Court along with copy of Final Report under section 279/338/304A IPC &
185 M.V. Act.

It is well settled law that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. sentences.text: It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied...."

23. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 by holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
